meta.title: Armbian — Optimized Linux for 300+ ARM Boards
meta.description: Production-ready Debian and Ubuntu images with patched kernels for ARM single board computers. Tested releases, automated builds, vendor-neutral.

hero.subtitle: Production-ready Debian and Ubuntu for ARM hardware. Every image ships with a patched kernel, tested drivers, and automated builds — so your board works out of the box.

philosophy.label: Why Armbian?
philosophy.title: More than a Linux image.
philosophy.subtitle: ARM hardware is fragmented. Every board ships with a different kernel, different patches, different quirks. Armbian unifies all of it into a single, tested, reproducible platform.
philosophy.base_description: Built on clean upstream repositories. Full APT ecosystem, systemd, thousands of packages — no vendor forks, no proprietary layers, no surprises.
philosophy.kernels_description: Every board gets a kernel tuned for its specific SoC. We apply Device Tree fixes, backport drivers, and test peripherals — so GPU, networking, and GPIO work on first boot.
philosophy.ecosystem_description: Home servers, industrial gateways, kiosks, dev environments. Pick a minimal CLI image or a full desktop — Armbian adapts to the job.

catalog.title: Supported Hardware
catalog.subtitle: 300+ boards from 60+ manufacturers. Every image is built, tested, and maintained by the community.

build.label: Build Framework
build.description: Compile an entire OS image with a single command. Kernel, bootloader, root filesystem, packages — fully automated and byte-for-byte reproducible for any supported board.
build.feature_1_desc: Same interface for every SoC. No per-vendor toolchains or SDK installs.
build.feature_2_desc: Choose your kernel branch, desktop environment, packages, and output format.
build.feature_3_desc: Same source, same config, same output. Deterministic builds, every time.
build.feature_4_desc: Entire build runs in containers. Zero host contamination.

deploy.title: Get started.
deploy.subtitle: Two paths to run Armbian. Choose the one that fits your workflow.
deploy.imager_description: The fastest way to get running. Pick your board, select an image, and flash directly to SD card or USB drive. Armbian Imager handles download, SHA verification, and writing in one step. No terminal needed. Available for Windows, macOS, and Linux.
deploy.manual_description: Full control over the process. Browse the catalog, pick the image format that fits your target — SD card, QEMU, Hyper-V or rootfs tarball — verify the GPG signature, then flash or import with the right tool. Every release ships with checksums and signed metadata.

donation.title: Support Armbian
donation.message: Armbian is 100% volunteer-run. If it saves you time, consider giving back.

donate_page.hero_subtitle: Armbian is built entirely by volunteers. Your contribution directly funds kernel development, hardware testing, build infrastructure, and community support across hundreds of ARM boards.
donate_page.why_1_desc: Every board needs patched kernels, Device Tree fixes, and driver backports. This is the most time-intensive work we do.
donate_page.why_2_desc: Automated builds, CI pipelines, and download mirrors run 24/7. Servers and bandwidth cost real money.
donate_page.why_3_desc: Forums, documentation, and moderation are volunteer-driven. Resources help us respond faster and write better guides.
donate_page.why_4_desc: Bringing up new hardware takes weeks of reverse engineering, driver work, and testing by skilled developers.
donate_page.method_github_desc: Monthly or one-time sponsorship through GitHub. The most direct way to fund recurring development.
donate_page.method_paypal_desc: One-time or recurring donations via PayPal.
donate_page.method_liberapay_desc: Recurring donations through the open-source Liberapay platform.
donate_page.method_merch_desc: Wear the brand. Armbian t-shirts and gear that fund the project.
donate_page.method_partnership_desc: Become an official hardware partner and get your boards supported by Armbian.
donate_page.other_code: Contribute code — kernel patches, drivers, and board support packages.
donate_page.other_docs: Write docs — setup guides, tutorials, and translations.
donate_page.other_test: Test releases — report bugs and verify fixes on your hardware.
donate_page.other_community: Help others — answer questions in the forum and community channels.
